title: Human Physiology for Engineers
description: Quantitative homeostasis across excitable, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, and endocrine systems, with emphasis on feedback and transport.

modifications: Linked the first four lesson objectives to outcomes, clarified the homeostasis objective, corrected the membrane-voltage item association, and added direct practice for feedback-loop components, membrane voltage as a state variable, and ventilation limitation.

prerequisites.statement: Cell biology; Physics: Mechanics; calculus recommended

outcomes.description: Use mass and energy balance to describe homeostasis.
Connect membrane transport to organ-level function.

lesson_objectives.description: Represent a regulated variable, sensor, controller, and effector, and use a simple balance to describe homeostasis.
Distinguish negative from positive feedback.
Interpret membrane voltage as an electrical state variable.
Relate ionic conductance to current and reversal potential.
Use pressure-flow resistance analogies with stated assumptions.
Distinguish ventilation, perfusion, and diffusion limitation.
Use clearance and balance concepts to interpret kidney function.
Predict how hormonal feedback changes transport or set points.
Calculate arterial and venous oxygen content from hemoglobin, saturation and partial pressure.
Apply the Fick principle to compute cardiac output, oxygen delivery and the extraction ratio.
Predict how anemia and changes in cardiac output alter delivery and extraction, and which compensations are available.
Calculate clearance from urine concentration, urine flow and plasma concentration, and use suitable markers to estimate GFR and renal plasma flow.
Compute filtered load and predict urinary excretion of a reabsorbed solute with a transport maximum.
Infer net tubular secretion or reabsorption by comparing a substance's clearance with GFR, and evaluate the limits of creatinine-based estimates.
Calculate net filtration pressure from hydrostatic and oncotic pressures with a reflection coefficient using the Starling equation.
Compute a filtration rate from the filtration coefficient and net pressure, and predict where along a capillary fluid leaves or returns.
Predict how changes in capillary pressure, plasma protein or wall permeability shift fluid balance, and explain the role of lymph.
Compute the steady state, time constant and approach time of a well-mixed compartment from a mass balance.
Estimate heat production from oxygen uptake and the rate of temperature rise from an energy imbalance.
Calculate closed-loop deviation and loop gain, and distinguish a shifted set point from a failure of regulation.
Calculate the Nernst equilibrium potential of an ion from its concentrations on either side of the membrane.
Compute a resting membrane potential from relative permeabilities with the Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz equation, and as a conductance-weighted average of reversal potentials.
Predict how a change in extracellular potassium shifts the resting potential, and explain why it changes less than the potassium equilibrium potential does.
Compute cardiac output, total peripheral resistance and the flow through a parallel organ bed from pressures and resistances.
Apply Poiseuille's relation to predict how radius changes alter resistance and flow.
Use compliance to relate stroke volume to pulse pressure, and estimate mean arterial pressure from systolic and diastolic values.
Interpret a ventricular pressure-volume loop's width and use a stated pressure-volume approximation to estimate stroke volume and external stroke work.
Compute minute and alveolar ventilation from tidal volume, breathing rate and dead space, and explain why shallow rapid breathing is less effective.
Apply the alveolar gas equation and the relation between alveolar CO₂, CO₂ production and alveolar ventilation.
Calculate lung–chest wall compliance and a shunt fraction, and predict the effects of stiff lungs and of shunt on gas exchange.
Compute the maximum isometric force of a muscle from its physiological cross-sectional area and specific tension.
Use the length–tension relation and Hill's force–velocity equation to compute force, velocity and power.
Predict how a loss of cross-sectional area changes force and power, and state what the model leaves out.
Order the phases of skin wound healing, name their main cell types and compare their time scales.
Compute closure time, percent closed and migration speed from a front-migration model, and a half-time from an exponential model.
Evaluate what a closure assay in culture can and cannot show about healing in a tissue.
Summarize repeated closure measurements by condition and time, counting independent experiments and averaging open area.
Calculate a closure rate, a relative closure and an edge migration speed from mean open area.
Evaluate which conclusions a closure assay with a migration inhibitor and a division block supports about migration, division and healing.
Calculate how a held arterial pressure is achieved by a different combination of output and resistance, and what that does to the flow through an individual organ bed.
Quantify reserve as the difference between maximum capacity and current use, and show how compensation uses it up.
Design a perturbation or an independent measurement that reveals reduced reserve behind a normal resting value.
Treat a patch of membrane as a resistor and capacitor in parallel, calculate its time constant and a small cell's input resistance, and predict the voltage response to a current step.
Calculate the length constant of a cylindrical process from membrane and axial resistances and predict steady-state electrotonic decay with distance.
Explain how fiber radius and myelination change the length constant and conduction velocity, and distinguish passive spread from a regenerated action potential.
Write the membrane equation for a uniformly polarized patch of membrane, and explain how a voltage clamp separates and measures the ionic currents.
Compute a gating variable's steady state and time constant from its opening and closing rates, its relaxation after a voltage step, and the resulting conductance and current.
Explain the upstroke, repolarization, undershoot, threshold and refractory period of an action potential from the different speeds of the m, h and n gates.
Use a filtration-only reference to infer a model filtration rate with explicit units.
Compare filtered load, excretion and fractional excretion without confusing concentrations and rates.
Infer a net transport direction while identifying what a steady-state ledger cannot resolve.
Reconcile glucose excretion with a stipulated transport maximum and its sharp-threshold limit.
Communicate a model ledger without converting synthetic inputs into a health conclusion.
Propagate a conserved filtered-solute amount through serial segments.
Combine separate water and sodium ledgers to obtain urine concentration.
Distinguish a water-permeability perturbation from a solute-removal perturbation.
Connect membrane transport controls with the limits of a segment ledger.
Solve a coupled balance/control equilibrium and initial derivative.
Distinguish damped eigenmodes from general physiological stability.
Check a saturated equilibrium against its active branch.
Separate sensor bias from loss of control reserve.
Mix conserved oxygen content across parallel blood streams.
Demonstrate the noncommutation of nonlinear binding conversion and averaging.
Close oxygen delivery, tissue uptake and extraction ledgers.
Distinguish an equivalent mixing fraction from unique mechanism evidence.
Verify a passive step using units, initial slope and analytic response.
Propagate a fixed-rate gate and distinguish conductance, current and passive spatial attenuation.
Verify nonlinear mixed content and separate oxygen delivery from uptake.
Couple parallel resistance and oxygen ledgers without inferring a unique bypass.
Build separate serial sodium and water balances for a distinct nephron model.
Keep independent water and solute perturbations distinct.
Verify equilibrium, modal decay and the initial balance before numerical simulation.
Separate loss of reserve from sensor bias and interpret normalized states.

duration.equivalent_structure: Proposed 14-week undergraduate scope only. Two compact prototype units remain in weeks 5 and 11 beside original lessons on balance and feedback, membrane potential, hemodynamics, respiratory mechanics, oxygen delivery, capillary exchange, muscle mechanics and tissue repair; week 13 is a synthetic-data closure lab and week 14 a compensation-and-reserve lesson with the course case. All activities are open, ungraded practice. There are no graded homework sets, exams or project, and workload has not been measured, so this schedule is not evidence of semester equivalence.

weeks.title: Homeostasis as balance: mass balance, energy balance and feedback gain
Excitable cells: driving force, gating and the Hodgkin–Huxley action potential
Membrane potential and passive cable properties
Hemodynamics: pressure, flow, resistance and compliance
Oxygen delivery and the Fick principle
Fluid exchange across capillaries and edema
Skeletal muscle mechanics: length, velocity and power
Renal, endocrine and integrated regulation; renal clearance; optional renal-clearance ledger project
Tissue repair: phases of healing and closure kinetics
Virtual lab: closure kinetics in a scratch assay
Compensation and reserve: how a regulated value can hide impaired capacity

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Homeostasis and feedback
lessons.worked_example: In the constructed balance dC/dt=r/V−kC, input 12 µmol/min into 2 L with k=0.3 min⁻¹ gives steady concentration 20 µmol/L. The response time is 1/k=3.33 min, after which 36.8% of a small initial deviation remains under this first-order model.

lessons.title: Excitable cells and electrophysiology
lessons.worked_example: With outward-positive current, Vm=−60 mV, EK=−90 mV and gK=2 nS give IK=+60 pA. With gNa=0.2 nS at ENa=+50 mV and gK=2 nS at EK=−90 mV, the passive zero-current voltage is about −77.3 mV, where the two ionic currents balance.

lessons.title: Cardiovascular and respiratory transport
lessons.worked_example: An ideal tube carrying 0.50 mL/s would carry 8.0 mL/s if radius doubled at fixed pressure drop, length and viscosity; the sixteenfold result is a model scaling, not a biological prediction.

lessons.title: Renal, endocrine, and integrated regulation
lessons.worked_example: For urine concentration 50 mg/L, urine flow 1 mL/min and plasma concentration 2 mg/L, convert flow to 0.001 L/min. Excretion is 0.05 mg/min, so clearance is 0.025 L/min or 25 mL/min; this constructed example emphasizes unit consistency, not a clinical estimate.

modules.title: Oxygen delivery and the Fick principle

lessons.title: Oxygen delivery: arterial content, the Fick principle and extraction
lessons.worked_example: C_a = 1.34 × 15 × 0.98 + 0.003 × 100 = 20.0 mL/dL; C_v = 15.20 mL/dL; Q̇ = 250/48.0 = 5.21 L/min; DO₂ = 1041 mL/min; extraction 0.24, rising to 0.36 at Hb 10 g/dL with unchanged flow.

lessons.title: Renal clearance: measuring filtration, plasma flow and tubular handling
lessons.worked_example: GFR = 30 × 1.0/0.25 = 120 mL/min; RPF ≈ C_PAH = 600 mL/min; FF = 0.20; glucose at 4.0 mg/mL: load 480 mg/min, excretion 105 mg/min; drug X clearance 60 mL/min (net reabsorption).

lessons.title: Fluid exchange across capillaries: Starling forces, filtration, absorption and why edema forms
lessons.worked_example: With P_i = 0 mmHg, π_c = 25 mmHg, π_i = 5 mmHg and σ = 0.9, the net filtration pressure is 17 mmHg at P_c = 35 and -3 mmHg at P_c = 15; at a mean 25 mmHg and K_f = 0.5, filtration is 3.5 mL/min; lowering π_c to 15 raises the arterial-end net pressure to 26 mmHg.

lessons.title: Homeostasis as balance: mass balance, energy balance and the gain of negative feedback
lessons.worked_example: With V = 14 L, clearance 7 L/h and production 35 mmol/h, C_ss = 5 mmol/L with τ = 2 h; halving clearance doubles C_ss and τ; 1.5 L/min of oxygen gives 30 kJ/min, and an imbalance of 19 kJ/min warms a 70 kg body by 0.078 °C/min; a disturbance of 10 with loop gain 4 leaves 2.

lessons.title: Membrane potential: the Nernst potential, the Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz equation and why extracellular potassium matters
lessons.worked_example: E_K = -89.1 mV and E_Na = +66.6 mV; GHK with P_K : P_Na = 1 : 0.04 gives -68.6 mV; raising K⁺ to 8 mM shifts E_K by 12.6 mV but the resting potential by only 6.6 mV (-62.0 mV); the conductance-weighted average with g_Na = 0.15 g_K is -68.8 mV.

lessons.title: Hemodynamics: pressure, flow, resistance and compliance
lessons.worked_example: With CO = 4.8 L/min, MAP = 100 and CVP = 4 mmHg, TPR = 20; beds of 40, 60 and 120 in parallel give 20; halving a radius multiplies resistance by 16; stiffening arteries to 1.2 mL/mmHg raises pulse pressure from 36 to 50 mmHg; dilating the muscle bed to 30 lowers TPR to 15.00 and would drop MAP to 76 mmHg unless output rises to 6.4 L/min. A separate synthetic PV rectangle with EDV 120 mL, ESV 50 mL and mean ejection pressure 100 mmHg gives SV 70 mL and about 0.933 J per beat; a stipulated perturbation to ESV 70 mL and pressure 120 mmHg gives SV 50 mL and about 0.800 J. This approximation is not a clinical estimate.

lessons.title: Respiratory mechanics and gas exchange: ventilation, dead space, compliance and the alveolar gas equation
lessons.worked_example: Alveolar ventilation is 4.2 L/min at V_T 500 mL and f 12, but only 2.4 L/min at 250 mL and 24 per minute; halving it doubles alveolar CO₂ to 82 mmHg; room-air P_AO₂ is 99.7 mmHg and falls to 49.7 mmHg with P_aCO₂ 80; series compliance of 50 and 200 is 40; contents 20.1, 19.0 and 15.2 give a shunt fraction of 0.22.

lessons.title: Skeletal muscle mechanics: sarcomere length, force–velocity and power
lessons.worked_example: A muscle of 20 cm² at 25 N/cm² has F₀ = 500 N; at a sarcomere length of 3.0 μm it produces 0.43 F₀; Hill's equation gives 6.67 cm/s at half load and 16.7 W, with peak power 19.1 W at 0.31 F₀; losing 30% of the area lowers peak power to 13.4 W.

lessons.title: Tissue repair: the phases of wound healing, scar versus regeneration and the kinetics of closure
lessons.worked_example: A 500 μm gap with edges advancing 25 μm/h each closes in 10 h (60% by 6 h), or in 16.7 h if the speed falls 40%; a 300 μm scratch 75% closed at 12 h implies 9.38 μm/h per edge and closure at 16 h; an exponential decay with k = 0.1 per hour has a half-time of 6.9 h.

lessons.title: Passive membrane and cable properties: time constant, length constant and conduction
lessons.worked_example: With R_m = 20 kΩ·cm² and C_m = 1 μF/cm², τ_m = 20 ms for any cell size; a 20 μm cell has R_in = 1.59 GΩ, so 10 pA gives 15.9 mV at steady state. An axon of radius 1 μm with R_i = 100 Ω·cm has λ = 1.0 mm, leaving 13.5% of a steady voltage at 2 mm. A dendrite (a = 0.5 μm, R_m = 40 kΩ·cm², R_i = 200 Ω·cm) has λ = 0.707 mm and τ_m = 40 ms, so a 10 mV synaptic depolarization 0.5 mm away arrives as 4.93 mV in the steady-state model.

modules.title: Virtual laboratory: closure kinetics in a scratch assay

lessons.title: Virtual lab 1: closure kinetics in a synthetic scratch assay
lessons.worked_example: Mean control open area falls to 47% by 12 h (4.42 points per hour), the migration inhibitor reaches 0.49 of control closure, and a 400 μm gap implies 8.83 μm/h per edge; blocking division leaves 0.97 of control closure at 24 h, so most closure is migration, within a flat culture that says nothing about healing in tissue.

lessons.title: Compensation and reserve: how a regulated value can hide impaired capacity
lessons.worked_example: Two synthetic people hold MAP at 100 mmHg, A with 4.8 L/min and B with 3.87 L/min through narrowed beds; B's gut-and-kidney flow is 0.4 L/min against 0.8, its extraction 0.32 against 0.26, and its reserve 0.63 against 3.2 L/min; dilating the muscle bed lets A hold pressure but drops B's MAP to 92 mmHg; heart-rate reserve gives maximum tolerable stroke-volume losses of 47% for A and 33% for B.

lessons.title: Voltage-gated conductances and the action potential: the Hodgkin–Huxley model
lessons.worked_example: After a clamp step to 0 mV with α_n = 0.552 and β_n = 0.0555 ms⁻¹, n relaxes from 0.318 toward 0.909 with τ_n = 1.65 ms; at 1 ms n = 0.587, g_K = 36 × 0.587⁴ ≈ 4.27 mS/cm² (about 11.6 times rest) and I_K ≈ 329 μA/cm² outward.

lessons.title: Renal-clearance ledger project guide (optional, ungraded)
lessons.worked_example: In a separate synthetic case, reference plasma 0.10 mg/mL, urine 4.5 mg/mL and flow 2.0 mL/min give GFR 90 mL/min. A solute with plasma 0.020 and urine 0.45 mg/mL has filtered load 1.8 and excretion 0.9 mg/min, so net reabsorption is 0.9 mg/min.

lessons.title: Nephron segments and regulated transport
lessons.worked_example: Convert 80 mL/min to 0.080 L/min before multiplying by 125 mmol/L: filtered sodium is 10 mmol/min. Sequential remaining fractions give 10×0.5×0.2×0.25×0.1=0.025 mmol/min. Fractional excretion is 0.0025; segment fractions refer to delivered, not original filtered, amount.

modules.title: Delayed feedback and a scaled water-balance model

lessons.title: Delayed feedback and a scaled water-balance model
lessons.worked_example: At equilibrium h=−w and 0=0.3−w+2h, hence w=0.1 and h=−0.1. Starting from zero states, wdot=0.3/3=0.1. Negative h means a signal deviation below its reference, not a negative absolute hormone concentration or a measured human response. Verify the declared amount and boundary equations independently before interpreting the result.

modules.title: Parallel gas exchange and nonlinear content mixing

lessons.title: Parallel gas exchange and nonlinear content mixing
lessons.worked_example: The common curve gives 162 and 90 mL O2/L. Oxygen amount rates add as 2×162+1×90=414 mL/min; dividing by total flow three gives mixed content 138. Averaging outlet pressures would skip the nonlinear binding conversion and generally violate this oxygen ledger.

lessons.title: Assignment 1: membrane and gating verification
lessons.worked_example: Cm/gL=5 ms and Vinf=EL+I/gL=−50 mV. The solution V=−60+10(1−exp(−t/5)) gives about −53.6788 mV at five milliseconds; its right-hand initial slope is 2 mV/ms. This passive current step is separate from the assignment voltage-clamp gate experiment. Verify the declared amount and boundary equations independently before interpreting the result.

lessons.title: Assignment 2: gas-flow and evidence report
lessons.worked_example: The two outlet contents are 180 and 100, yielding mixed content (3×180+100)/4=160 mL/L. The inverse pressure is 25 sqrt(160/40)=50, while delivery is 640 and uptake 320 mL/min. Averaging the pressures instead would give 62.5 and would not preserve the oxygen-content ledger.

lessons.title: Assignment 3: nephron ledger and perturbations
lessons.worked_example: Filtered amount is 0.090×120=10.8 mmol/min. Sodium remaining is 10.8×0.5×0.25×0.2×0.1=0.027, or fraction 0.0025. Water remaining is 90×0.4×0.5×1×0.1=1.8 mL/min; converting to liters before dividing gives urine sodium 15 mmol/L. Verify the declared amount and boundary equations independently before interpreting the result.

lessons.title: Assignment 4: delayed feedback and reserve
lessons.worked_example: Steady balance gives w=0.3/(1+2)=0.1 and h=−0.2. The characteristic equation is 2lambda²+3lambda+3=0, giving −3/4±i sqrt(15)/4. Initially wdot=0.3/2=0.15 and hdot=0. These analytic checks constrain a numerical report without asserting any measured physiological time course. Verify the declared amount and boundary equations independently before interpreting the result.

grading_policy.attempt_policy: Unlimited formative retries; no summative grade is awarded.
grading_policy.solution_release: Public practice solutions may be shown after an attempt. They are not production exam keys.
grading_policy.late_policy: No deadlines or late penalties exist in this partial package.
grading_policy.appeals: No instructor review workflow is implemented; report ambiguous practice items to repository maintainers.

accessibility.diagram_policy: The seed package contains no imported diagrams; newly authored diagrams require descriptions and individual license tracking.
known_issues: Unicode equations require structured mathematical alternatives and assistive-technology review.

history.summary: Preserved original compact prototype content in separate manifests and readings; labeled partial without semester or credit equivalency.

Added two original lessons (oxygen content, the Fick principle, delivery and extraction, and renal clearance, filtration and tubular handling) with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.
Added an original lesson on capillary Starling forces, filtration and edema with synthetic data, formative items with computed keys and retrieval cards. The package remains partial and unreviewed.

Assessments with items now also list the course outcomes those items assess, derived from each item's lesson objective and that objective's outcome links. The rubric-only case lists none, and neither do the 4 prototype-unit assessments, whose objectives are not yet linked to an outcome. No readings, items or keys changed. The syllabus was regenerated from the manifest: it states the current version, lists every lesson with its item and card counts, and describes the current practice and limitations (it still described only the four original units). The course limitations shown to learners were also updated: they still described one formative check per lesson and the original numerical rules. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a common-mistakes section to 2 original lessons that lacked one (physiology-5, physiology-6); each bullet names a mistake that the lesson's own text addresses. No answer key, tolerance or objective changed. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a proposed 14-week schedule; seven original lessons (balance and feedback gain with heat balance; membrane potential with the Nernst and Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz equations; hemodynamics; respiratory mechanics and gas exchange; skeletal muscle mechanics with Hill's force–velocity relation; tissue repair and closure kinetics; and compensation and reserve, which prepares the course case); and a synthetic-data scratch-assay lab with a migration inhibitor and a division block. No new references were added. All activities remain ungraded practice; the package remains partial and unreviewed, gives no medical advice, and makes no claim about any person.

Expanded the week-1 homeostasis reading with amount balance, a first-order concentration model, negative-feedback direction and a response-time calculation. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Three compact prototype readings remain; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-3 electrophysiology reading with membrane-voltage and current conventions, ionic driving force, pathway conductances and a multi-ion steady-state calculation. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. Two compact prototype readings remain; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-5 transport reading with pressure-flow resistance, series and parallel pathways, diffusion across an exchange surface, regional ventilation-perfusion matching and transport-limitation distinctions. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. One compact prototype reading remains; the package stays partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Expanded the week-11 renal and endocrine reading with clearance units, filtered-load balance, limits of clearance comparisons, feedback sensitivity and integrated amount balance. Existing questions, keys and objectives are unchanged. All four original compact prototype readings now have expanded primers; the package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Linked the first four lesson objective pairs to the matching course outcomes, clarified the homeostasis objective, corrected the membrane-voltage question association, and added direct formative checks for feedback-loop components, membrane voltage, and ventilation limitation. Existing numeric prompts and keys are unchanged. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an inactive, ungraded synthetic renal-clearance ledger draft that reconciles clearance, filtered load, excretion and net tubular handling; linked it from the syllabus while keeping platform activation off. Existing lessons, practice items, keys and cards are unchanged. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only; the invented quantities are not clinical measurements.

Expanded the existing hemodynamics lesson with a synthetic ventricular pressure-volume loop, stroke-volume comparison, external stroke-work calculation and model limitations. Added one objective, six formative items and four retrieval cards without adding a week. The values are invented and are not clinical estimates; the course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added an original passive membrane and cable-properties reading grouped with the week-4 membrane-potential lesson: the membrane as a parallel RC element, the size-independent time constant and compact-cell input resistance, the core-conductor length constant and electrotonic decay, conduction-velocity scaling with radius and myelination, and passive spread versus regenerated action potentials. MIT OCW 6.021J Fall 2004 (core-conductor, cable and myelinated-fiber lectures) is registered as a link-only comparator. Three objectives, ten formative items and four cards; no week was added. The course remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Added a Hodgkin–Huxley reading to week 3: the membrane equation, voltage clamp, gating variables and their kinetics, conductances from n⁴ and m³h, and threshold, spike shape and refractoriness explained by gate speeds, with numbers computed from the classic model. Eight numeric and four choice items, four retrieval cards, a practice assessment and independent recalculation tests were added; stale numeric-answer and significant-figure counts in the limitations were corrected. The package remains partial, unreviewed and formative-only.

Made the planned renal-clearance ledger project usable as optional ungraded practice: an original guide, a separate worked example and rehearsal, 5 open practice items and 5 private Case studio milestone self-checks. Pinned learner datasets locally. The inactive review draft stays separate; the package remains partial and unreviewed.

Added three original nephron segment, delayed feedback and nonlinear parallel gas-exchange foundations, four connected membrane/gating, gas-flow, nephron and feedback reports, and twenty checkpoints/cards. Corrected the nonzero initial n^4 conductance slope and stale syllabus/cable scope statements. Synthetic models remain partial, unreviewed and formative-only; no real measurements or laboratory competence claimed.

limitations: Practice items are short formative checks (two or three per prototype unit and six to twelve per expanded lesson); the hemodynamics lesson has thirteen because it also includes a bounded cardiac pressure-volume addition. These items do not demonstrate comprehensive outcome coverage or mastery, and objective associations remain provisional.
Bloom labels and structured prerequisite edges are initial authoring classifications awaiting subject-matter review.
Question answers and solution feedback are intentionally public practice authoring specifications, not restricted exam keys.
Total workload and weekly duration are unknown; former nominal credit values and hardcoded reading times do not establish workload.
All physiological scenarios, people and numbers are synthetic teaching examples; this package gives no medical advice, describes no real person's health and recommends no test or treatment.

The optional renal-clearance ledger project is ungraded. Its milestone drafts are private self-checks; no software check evaluates the learner’s written derivation, diagram or interpretation. The proposed schedule and time estimate have not been measured.

The first two prototype units remain concise primers; later transport/renal prototypes have longer explanations. Three new foundations and four connected open assignments deepen nephron transport, delayed feedback, nonlinear content mixing and membrane verification. One synthetic-data virtual lab does not replace an experimental laboratory sequence. No active graded homework, midterm, cumulative final or project exists; workload and qualified review remain open.

Nephron fractions, scaled controller parameters and the oxygen-binding curve are invented teaching inputs, not human measurements or validated physiological estimates. Target clipping differs from clipping numerical states. Equivalent bypass fractions and regulated values do not uniquely identify real mechanisms. Browser checkpoints do not score solver code, proofs, reports or proposed investigations.

Of the 150 numerical answers, 36 require units, 72 check significant figures and 0 check dimensions. New continuous checkpoint quantities request three significant figures. Written reports and interpretations beyond selected fields are not automatically evaluated.
intentionally_omitted: Graded assessments and a laboratory sequence are not authored yet (one synthetic-data virtual lab exists); the original lessons extend a partial package.
The synthetic renal-clearance ledger is an inactive, ungraded paper-exercise draft and is not activated or mapped to course completion.
